nodes.statement: Let T=(T,sigma,1) be a tile assembly system such that the seed assembly sigma is finite and connected. There is a constant c(|T|,|domsigma|) such that any path P, that can grow in all assemblies of T and reaches a point at a distance more than c(|T|,sigma) from sigma, is pumpable.

nodes.name: Pumpability

If Q is a path assembly, since P_[ind1,ind2] is not pumpable then there exists a conflict between Q and sigma cup P_[1,ind2]. In this case, the lemma is true. Otherwise if Q is not a path assembly, for the sake of contradiction suppose that Q_ind3 notin domsigma cup P_[1,ind2]. Then there exists 1 leq ind4 < ind3 such that pos(Q_ind3)=pos(Q_ind4) and type(Q_ind3) neq type(Q_ind4). Let ell=|P_[ind1,ind2]|-1 and ensuremathoverrightarrowv be the direction of P_[ind1,ind2]. If ell<ind4 then by fact , we have Q_ind3-ell=Q_ind3-ensuremathoverrightarrowv and Q_ind4-ell=Q_ind4-ensuremathoverrightarrowv. Then there exists a conflict between Q_ind3-ell and Q_ind4-ell which contradicts the definition of ind3. If ind4 leq ell then by fact and by definition of Q, there exists ind1 leq ind5 leq ind2 such that P_ind5=Q_ind4-ensuremathoverrightarrowv. nodes.statement: The proof of the main result is long, difficult and requires a lot of transitional lemmas. These lemmas are gathered into different parts as shown in Figure (these dependencies do not introduce a cycle). Note that, all results of this paper can be categorized in two categories: microscopic and macroscopic ones. Microscopic results focus on a local part of an assembly. A simple typical example is "a segment of |T|+1 tiles of an assembly contains at least two identical tiles". On the one hand, these results requires no prerequisites but on the other hand, they deal with very specific conditions (i.e. a long list of hypothesis), they are not very useful alone and their proofs are technical and could lead to an explosion of cases to study if not done carefully. Thus microscopic reasoning is lengthy, tedious, technical and not intuitive. Macroscopic results zoom out and focus on the whole assembly.

nodes.statement: In a first time, we will focus on the four first properties, we will deal with the two conventions at the end. By hypothesis there exists an index 1leq ind1 leq |P| such that the distance between pos(P_ind1) and the seed is at least B^f+1. Moreover, since P is producible by T=(T,sigma,1) then there exists an index 1leq ind2 leq |P| such that pos(P_ind2) in domsigma. Suppose that ind1<ind2 (the other case is symmetric and simpler), see Figure a for graphical representation of the following notations, then let ind3= min_ind1 leq i leq ind2\i :pos(P_i) in domsigma\ and ind4=max_ind1 leq i leq ind3\i :pos(P_i) is at distance B^f+1 of the seed\. Now, let P' be the path assembly such that for all 1leq i leq ind4-ind3+1, we have P'_i=P_ind4-i+1 (P' is obtained by switching the indexing of the segment P_[ind4,ind3], see Figure b). Now, if P' is not simple then there exist two indices 1< ind5 < ind6 < |P'| such that P_ind5=P_ind6 then let P''=P_[1,ind5] cdot P_[ind6,|P'|] (see Figure a). W. l. o.g, we suppose that the path assembly P'' is simple (other cycles could be removed the same way). Then alpha_P'' sqsubseteq alpha_P, and domP'' cap domsigma= pos(P'_1) and then P'' is producible by T. This means that if P'' is pumpable or fragile then P is pumpable or fragile. Moreover P'' is finite (|P''| leq |P'| leq ind4-ind3+1), simple and P''_|P''| is the only tile of P'' which is at distance more than B^f+1 of the seed. If there exists 0 leq j leq ell such that A_1 in V(D^j) then by lemma , since P is simple and since by hypothesis V(P) cap V(W') subset \P_ind2\, then we have A_1=P_ind2. Moreover by lemma , either P_ind2=D^k_1=S^k_|S^k| or P_ind2=D^k_|D^k|=S^k+1_1. If ind3 >m then let 1leq ind0 leq ind1 such that P_ind0=A^i_1 and thus the arc P_[ind0,ind1] dominates A^i which is a contradiction.

nodes.statement: This proof is made by a local reasoning along tile P_ind1. First, consider the special case where ind1=1 then i=1, |A^1|=1. Moreover the window associated to A^1 is W and then G^I=G_2 and G_3=G_1 and the edge (P_1,P_2) belongs either to G_3 or to G^I. Otherwise, we supposer that A^i is positive (the other case is symmetric) since P_ind1=A^i_|A^i| then there exists ind2 such that P_ind1=W_ind2. Now, among the neighbors of P_ind1, there are P_ind1-1, P_ind1+1, W_ind2-1 and W_ind2+1. Since W is simple then W_ind1-1 neq W_ind1+1 and since the arc A^i is positive then it ends in W_ind2 and thus W_ind2+1 neq P_ind1-1 and W_ind2+1 neq P_ind1+1. Without loss of generality we can assume that W_ind2+1=W_ind2+(0,1). Since P_ind1-1 neq P_ind1+1 we are left with eighteen cases to study. This cases are classified in three categories: Edge (P_ind1,P_ind1+1) belongs to E(G^I): see Figure . A typical example of this case occurs when W_ind2-1=W_ind2-(1,0), P_ind1+1=P_ind1+(1,0) and P_ind1-1=P_ind1-(0,1). In this case, consider the window W' of G^I. Either W' is a finite cycle if j<ell' or W' is a the window associated to P_[1,ind1] if i=ell'. In both cases, there exists ind3 such that W'_ind3=W_ind2, W'_ind3+1=W_ind2+1 and W'_ind3-1=P_ind1-1 and G^I is the right side of W'. In this case, the edge (P_ind1,P_ind1+1) is on the right side of W'_[ind3-1,ind3+1] and thus this edge belong to G^I. The lemma is true in this case. vspace+0.5em Edge (P_ind1,P_ind1+1) belongs to E(G_3): see Figure . A typical example of this case occurs when W_ind2-1=W_ind2+(1,0), P_ind1+1=P_ind1-(1,0) and P_ind1-1=P_ind1-(0,1). In this case, consider the window W'' associated to the decomposition (A^i)_1leq i leq ell, we suppose that G_3 is the left side of W'' and thus G_3 is a subgraph of G_1. With these conventions, there exists ind4 such that W''_ind4=W_ind2, W''_ind4+1=W_ind2+1 and either W''_ind4-1=P_ind1-1 if the edge (P_ind1-1,P_ind1) belongs to E(G_1) or W''_ind4-1=W_ind2-1 otherwise (in this case |A^i|=1). In this case, the edge (P_ind1,P_ind1+1) is on the left side of W''_[ind4-1,ind4+1] and thus this edge belong to G_3. The lemma is true in this case. vspace+0.5em Arc A^i is a negative arc of length 1: see the combination of the two dotted neighborhood of Figure . This case occurs only time when W_ind2-1=W_ind2-(1,0), P_ind1+1=P_ind1-(0,1) and P_ind1-1=P_ind1+(1,0). In this case, by definition , the arc A^i is a negative arc of length 1 which contradicts the hypothesis that A^i is positive.

We suppose that P_[ind3,ind4] is positive (the other case is symmetric) then A^i and A^j are both positive. By contradiction suppose that ind1>ind2. See Figure a for an illustration of this setting. We distinguish three cases, ind3 leq ind2, ind2 < ind1 leq ind3 and ind2 leq ind3 leq ind1. The last case generates two sub-cases. We now show that they all lead to a contradiction. vspace+0.5em Case ind3 leq ind2: see Figure b for an illustration of this case. In this case, consider the decomposition (B^i)_1leq i leq ell' of P_[ind3,ind2] and let (D^i)_0leq i leq ell' be the dual decomposition of W associated to (B^i)_1leq i leq ell'. Note that, there exists 1leq k leq ell' such that B^k=A^j. Let G^I be the interior of D^k. Since ind2<ind1 then ind2<|P| and since B^k is positive, then by lemma the edge (P_ind2,P_ind2+1) belongs to E(G^I). Moreover, since i<j there exists k'<k such that P_ind1 in D^k'. Moreover since ind3<ind1 then k' geq 1. By definition of P_ind3, we have V(D^0) cap V(P_[ind2+1,ind1])=emptyset and then there exists no arc which starts in D^0 and ends in D^ell' and which is a subgraph of P_[ind2+1,ind1]. Moreover, since P is simple then P_[ind2+1,ind1] does not intersect with P_[ind3,ind2]. Then by applying lemma on (B^i)_1leq i leq ell' and P_[ind2+1,ind1], there exists an arc A which dominates B^k=A^j and which is a subgraph of P_[ind2+1,ind1] which is a contradiction. vspace+0.5em Case ind2 < ind1 leq ind3: see Figure c for an illustration of this case. In this case, let 1 leq ind5 leq |P| be such that P_ind5=A^j_1 then ind5leq ind2 and consider the decomposition (B^i)_1leq i leq ell' of P_[ind5,ind1] and let (D^i)_0leq i leq ell' be the dual decomposition of W associated to (B^i)_1leq i leq ell'. Note that, there exists 1leq i' leq j' leq ell' such that B^i'=A^i and B^j'=A^j. Let G^I be the interior of D^i'. Since ind1<ind4 then ind1<|P| and since B^i' is positive, then by lemma the edge (P_ind1,P_ind1+1) belongs to E(G^I). Moreover, by definition of ind4, we have P_ind4 in D^ell' and then there exists ind6=min\i>ind5:P_i in D^0 or D^ell'\. By definition of ind6, there exists no arc which starts in D^0 and ends in D^ell' and which is a subgraph of P_[ind1+1,ind6]. Moreover, since P is simple then P_[ind1+1,ind6] does not intersect with P_[ind5,ind1]. Then by applying lemma on (B^i)_1leq i leq ell' and P_[ind1+1,ind6], if P_ind6 in V(D^0) (resp. V(D^ell')) then there exists an arc A which dominates B^i'=A^i (resp. B^j'=A^j) and which is a subgraph of P_[ind2+1,ind6] which is a contradiction. vspace+0.5em Case ind2 leq ind3 leq ind1: in this case, let 1 leq ind5 leq |P| be such that P_ind5=A^j_1, then ind5leq ind2 and let 1leq ind6 leq |P| such that P_ind6=A^1_|A^1|. By definition of ind3 we have either A^1_1=P_ind3 (if A^1 is positive) or A^1_|A^1|=P_ind3 (if A^1 is negative), in both cases we have ind6geq ind3. We have ind6<ind4 otherwise A^1 would dominate A^i and A^j and then ind6 < |P|. Now, consider the decomposition (B^i)_1leq i leq ell' of P_[ind5,ind6] and let (D^i)_0leq i leq ell' be its dual decomposition of W. Note that A^1=B^1 and that there exists 1leq k leq ell' such that B^k=A^j. Now, we distinguish two subcases either B^1 is positive or negative. vspace+0.5em Sub-case B^1 is positive: see Figure d for an illustration of this case. Let G^I be the interior of D^1. Since B^1 is positive, then by lemma the edge (P_ind6,P_ind6+1) belongs to E(G^I). Moreover by definition of ind3, we have V(D^0) cap V(P_[ind6+1,ind4])=emptyset and then there exists no arc which starts in D^0 and ends in D^ell' and which is a subgraph of P_[ind6+1,ind4]. Moreover, since P is simple then P_[ind6+1,ind4] does not intersect with P_[ind5,ind6]. Also by definition of ind4, we have P_ind4 in V(D^ell'). Then by applying lemma on (B^i)_1leq i leq ell' and P_[ind6+1,ind4], there exists an arc A which dominates B^k=A^j and which is a subgraph of P_[ind6+1,ind4] which is a contradiction. vspace+0.5em Sub-case B^1 is negative: see Figure e for an illustration of this case. Moreover by definition of ind4, we have P_ind4 in V(D^ell'), then there exists ind7 = min \ i >ind6 : P_ind7 in V(D^ell')\. Note that since P is a simple path, then P_[ind6,ind7] is a subgraph of G^I. Moreover, since i<j there exists k'<k such that P_ind1 in D^k' and since ind3<ind1 then k' geq 1. Thus by lemma , we have ind7<ind1. By definition of P_ind3, we have V(D^0) cap V(P_[ind7,ind1])=emptyset and then there exists no arc which starts in D^0 and ends in D^ell' and which is a subgraph of P_[ind7,ind1]. Moreover, since P is a simple path then P_[ind7,ind1] does not intersect with P_[ind5,ind6]. Then by applying lemma on (B^i)_1leq i leq ell' and P_[ind7,ind1], there exists an arc A which dominates B^k=A^j and which is a subgraph of P_[ind7,ind1] which is a contradiction.

nodes.statement: This proof is done in three steps and relies on an algorithm to obtain the desired result. An example of this algorithm is illustrated in the Figures of appendix , the input of the algorithm is Figure . During the first step of the proof, we decompose the arc A into several elementary arcs to obtain a correct input for our algorithm (see Figure ). Now for each arc of this decomposition, the second step introduces a loop of the algorithm which modifies this arc (see Figures and for arc A^1 and Figure for arc A^2). The third step puts together all the different modified arcs of A to build the path R and proves that the path R matches the hypothesis of the lemma (see Figure ). Without loss of generality, we consider that G_1 is the left side of W and that G_1^+ is the right side of omeplusC. vspace+0.5em Input of the algorithm: consider the cut of the grid (C^+,C^-) associated to the periodic bi-infinite window W'=omeC. We suppose that C^+ is the right side of the cut. Let p=|C|-1 and consider an indexing of W' such that W'_0=C_1=A_1 and W'_p=C_|C|=A_|A|. Now let ind4=min\i: A_[ind4,|A|] is a subgraph of C^+\. Since A is a subgraph of G_1^+ then the edge (A_|A|-1,A_|A|) in E(C^+) and thus ind4<|A|. If ind4=1 then A is an arc of C^+ otherwise by contradiction suppose that 1< ind4 < |A|. Then, there exists ind5 such that A_ind4 = W'_ind5. Since A is a subgraph of G_1^+ then ind5<0 and then the width of A_[ind4,|A|] is strictly greater than p. Then, by lemma , A_[ind4,|A|] intersect with A_[ind4,|A|]+ensuremathoverrightarrowv which contradicts the fact that A is a good path. Then A is an arc of C^+. Now if A is not extremum then let A' be the extremum arc extracted from A. Similarly to the previous reasoning, the width of A' is strictly greater than p. Thus, arcs A' and A'+ensuremathoverrightarrowv intersect which is a contradiction. Thus A is an extremum positive arc of C^+. Now, consider a decomposition (A^i)_1leq i leq ell of A in elementary arcs in C^+ and its dual decomposition (D^i)_1leq i leq ell of W'. Then by lemma , there exists 0leq ind5 leq ind6leq p such that A=W'_[0,ind5] cdot_1leq i leq ell-1 (A^i cdot D^i)cdot A^ell cdot W'_[ind6,p]. Also remark that W'_[0,ind5] and W'_[ind6,p] are subpath of C and for all 1leq i leq ell, the dual segment D^i is a subpath of C. Remark that for all 1leq i leq ell, the path A^i is an arc of G_1^+. vspace+0.5em Shrinking an arc: Consider 1leq i leq ell, if for all kgeq 0 the path A^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv is a subgraph of G_1^+ then let B^i=A^i. Otherwise, there exists k>0 such that A^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv is not an elementary arc of G_1^+ then remark that A^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv cap V(omeplusC)=\A^i_1+kensuremathoverrightarrowv, A^i_|A^i|+kensuremathoverrightarrowv\ then A^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv is a basic path of G_1^+ which ends in A^i_|A^i|+kensuremathoverrightarrowv. Then by applying lemma on the basic path A^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv of G_1^+, there exists a basic arc B^i of G_1^+ such that the restrained interior B^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv is a subgraph of the restrained interior of A^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv, such that B^i_1=A^i_1, such that B^i_|B^i|=A^i_|A^i| and such that V(B^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv) cap V(W_[ind1+1,+infty]) neq emptyset. Then, there exists ind2>ind1 such that W_ind2 in B^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv and since y_ensuremathoverrightarrowvgeq 1 and since B^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv is a subgraph of the restrained interior of A^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv then y_W_ind2geq min\y_C,y_Q\+y_ensuremathoverrightarrowv. Also, B^i is a subgraph of the restrained interior of A^i which is a subgraph of G_1^+, then B is a subgraph of G_1^+. Remark that the number of edges of the restrained graph of B^i is strictly less than the number of edges in the restrained graph of A^i. By iterating this reasoning we can suppose for all kgeq 0, the arc B^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv is a subgraph of G_1^+. vspace+0.5em Iterating for all arcs: by doing the same reasoning for all elementary arcs, we obtain that a path R=W'_[0,ind5] cdot_1leq i leq ell-1 (B^i cdot D^i) cdot B^ell cdot W'_[ind6,p]. Now since for all 1leq i leq ell and for all k geq 0, the arc B^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv is a subgraph of the restrained interior of A^i+kensuremathoverrightarrowv and since A is a good path, then R is a good path. Moreover omeplusR is a subgraph of G_1^+. Now if R=Q then omeplusQ is a subgraph of G_1^+. Otherwise, there exists ind2>ind1 and ind3geq |R| such that omeplusR_ind3 =W_ind2 and such that y_W_ind2 geq min\y_C,y_Q\+y_ensuremathoverrightarrowv.

nodes.statement: See Figures and of appendix for a graphical representation of this proof. Since V(S) cap domsigma=emptyset and since the seed is connected then we can assume without loss of generality that domsigma subset V(lminkh). We start by localizing a candidate segment of the path assembly P of direction ensuremathoverrightarroww which is a subgraph of lminkh+1. Then using fact , we prove that either this segment is pumpable or that the path assembly P is fragile. Note that this is the only time in this article that we will try to pump a candidate segment which is not necessarily a good candidate segment. We start by proving the existence of indices 1leq kleq |M| and 1leq ind1 leq ind2 leq |P| such that: item there is no tile of the segment P_[ind1,ind2] positioned in lminkh, i.e. (domP_[ind1,ind2] cap V(lminkh)=emptyset); item the output glue of P_ind1-1 is M_k; item the output glue of P_ind2-1 is M'_k. Consider the following invariant I(k)="there exists 1leq ind1 leq ind2 leq |P| such that the output glue g_ind1-1 of P is M_k and the output glue g_ind2 of P is M'_k". First, we prove that H(1) is true. By hypothesis, the domain of the seed is in lminkh, i.e. domsigma subset V(lminkh) and thus h(pos(P_1)) < (h+1)p < (h'+1)p. Since the movies M and M' are not empty, consider the first index 1leq ind1 leq |P| such that the height of P_ind1 is greater than (h+1)p then the output glue g_ind1-1 of P is M_1. Similarly, consider the first index ind2 such that the height of P_ind2 is greater than (h'+1)p then the output glue g_ind2-1 of P is M'_1. Moreover h(P_ind2-1)geq (h'+1)p-max(x_ensuremathoverrightarrowv,y_ensuremathoverrightarrowv)>(h+1)p and thus we have ind1 leq ind2-1<ind2 and I(1) is true. Now, suppose that I(k) is true for 1leq k leq |M|-1. Then, there exists 1leq ind1 leq ind2 leq |P| such that the output glue g_ind1-1 of P is M_k and the output glue g_ind2 of P is M'_k. Two cases can occur: either domP_[ind1,ind2] cap V(lminkh)=emptyset and the desired indices ind1,ind2 and k have been found or P_[ind1,ind2] contains tiles positioned in lminkh. In the second case, there exists ind1leq ind3<ind2 such that h(P_ind3)< (h+1)p and since the output glue of P_ind2-1 is M'_k then either h(P_ind2)>(h'+1)p>(h+1)p or h(P_ind2-1)>(h'+1)p>(h+1)p, then there k'>k and ind3<ind4 leq ind2 such that the output glue g_ind4-1 of P is M_k'. By definition of a movie there exists ind5>ind4 such that the output glue of P_ind5-1 is M'_k' and this means that I(k') is true. Thus either we have found the desired index k or I(k') is true with k'>k. If I(|M|) is true then there exists 1leq ind1 leq ind2 leq |P| such that the output glue g_ind1-1 of P is M_|M| and the output glue g_ind2-1 of P is M'_|M|. If P_[ind1,ind2] contains positions of lminkh, then M_|M| could not be the last output glue of the movie which is a contradiction. Thus, the domain of the segment P_[ind1,ind2] cannot contain a vertex of lminkh and the desired indices ind1,ind2 and k=|M| have been found. Thus in all cases, there exist 1leq k leq |M| and 1leq ind1<ind2 leq |P| such that the output glue of P_ind1-1 is M_k, the output glue of P_ind2-1 is M'_k and domP_[ind1,ind2] cap V(lminkh-1)=emptyset. Moreover, since M'_k=M_k +ensuremathoverrightarroww and since the edges of the output glue are oriented then the direction of P_[ind1,ind2] is ensuremathoverrightarroww. Now, remark that the path assembly Q such that Q_[1,|Q|-1]=P_[1,ind2-1] and Q_|Q|=P_ind1+ensuremathoverrightarroww is a path assembly producible by T. Thus if type(P_ind2) neq type (P_ind1) then P is fragile. Then either P is fragile or P_[ind1,ind2] is a candidate segment of P of direction ensuremathoverrightarroww. If this candidate segment is pumpable then the lemma is true. Otherwise by lemma , there exists j>0 such that there exists a conflict between either P_[ind1,ind2]+jensuremathoverrightarroww and sigma or between P_[ind1,ind2]+jensuremathoverrightarroww and P_[1,ind2]. Now consider the sequence of assemblies (P^*i)_igeq 0 created by the window movie lemma (Lemma ). Then these assemblies are producible by T and by fact , P_[ind1,ind2]+jensuremathoverrightarroww is a subassembly of P^*j. Then P and P^*j are in conflict. Thus the path assembly P is fragile in this final case.

nodes.raw_latex: Consider the window $L^0$ and an indexing of $L^0$ such that for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, we have $L^0_{i+p}=L^0_i+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$, we will use this window and this indexing as a reference to compare different movies. Now, consider $h,h' \in \mathbb{Z}$, the two windows $L^{h}$ and $L^{h'}$ and the two non-empty movies $\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{M}(\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}},h)$ and $\mathcal{M}'=\mathcal{M}(\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}},h')$ of~$P$. There exist a vector $\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{w}}$ (resp. $\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{w}}'$) and an indexing of $L^{h}$ (resp. $L^{h'}$) such that $L^0+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{w}}=L^{h}$ (resp. $L^0+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{w}}'=L^{h'}$), such that $L^0_0+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{w}}=L^{h}_0$ (resp. $L^0_0+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{w}}=L^{h'}_0$) and such that $0\leq \min\{i \in \mathbb{Z}: L^{h}_i \in \dom{P}\} <p$ (resp. $0\leq \min\{i \in \mathbb{Z}: L^{h'}_i \in \dom{P}\} <p$); this fact is due to the periodicity of $L^{h}$ and $L^{h'}$, see Figure \ref{fig:uwl:simple}. If $\mathcal{M}^{h}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{w}}=\mathcal{M}^{h'}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{w}}'$ then these two movies are identical up to translation. Now, we enumerate the number of possible different movies. First, $\min\{i \in \mathbb{Z}: L^{h}_i \in \dom{P}\}$ can take $p$ different values. Since for all windows, the width of $\alpha_P$ is bounded by $c$ then there exists at most $c$ tiles of $P$ positioned on the window $L^{h}$. Any of these tiles can belong to at most two output glues of the movie $\mathcal{M}^{h}$. Then the size of all movies is bounded by $2c$. Now, there exists $(2c!)$ possible ways to order these $2c$ output glues. For each of this ordering there exists $(2|T|+1)^{2c}$ ways to color it (for this enumeration we consider the absence of an output glue has a type of glue and there is at most $|T|$ types of glues multiplied by two for the orientation of the edge). Then, there exists at most $p(2c!)(2|T|+1)^{2c}$ different movies up to translation. Now, there exists three kind of movies: the movies which contains output glues of the seed, the movies of height $h$ such that the domain of the seed is a subgraph of $\lmink{h}$ and the movies of height $h$ such that the domain of the seed is a subgraph of $\lplusk{h+1}$. There exists at most $|\sigma|$ movies of the first kind. Since the length of the movies is bounded by $2c$ and since $|P| \geq 4cp(2c!)(2|T|+1)^{2c}+2c|\sigma|$ then there exists at least $2p(2c!)(2|T|+1)^{2c}$ non-empty movies of the second or $2p(2c!)(2|T|+1)^{2c}$ non-empty movies of the third kind. Then, either there exists at least two movies of the second kind which are identical up to translation or there exists two movies of the third kind which are identical up to translation. Then by lemma \ref{lem:samemovie}, the path assembly $P$ is fragile or pumpable.

By contradiction, suppose that the width of $P$ is strictly greater than $2p^2+2p$. First, we show that without loss of generality we can consider that $P$ is an extremum finite path. Remark that if the width of $P$ is infinite, then it is possible to find a finite subpath of $P$ such that its width is strictly greater than $2p^2+2p$. Then, without loss of generality, we can suppose that $P$ is finite and such is its width. Now, consider an index of $L$ such that $0=\min\{i\in \mathbb{Z}: L_i \in V(P)\}$ and let $m=\max\{i\in \mathbb{Z}: L_i \in V(P)\}$ then the width of $P$ is $m>2p^2+2p$. Now, consider the extremum path extracted from $P$, 
this path is extremum and its width is $m$. Then, we can assume without loss of generality that $P$ is an extremum finite path of width strictly greater than $2p^2+2p$.

Let $Q=P-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ be the path $P$ translated by $-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$. Our aim is to prove that $P$ and $Q$ intersect. The path $Q$ starts in $L_{-p}=Q_1$ and ends in $L_{m-p}=Q_{|Q|}$. This proof will require to define eight indices. 


Consider the decomposition $(A^i)_{1\leq i \leq \ell}$ of $P$ in extremum arcs in $U$ and let $(S^i)_{0\leq i \leq \ell}$ be the decomposition of the window $L$ according to $(A^i)_{1\leq i \leq \ell}$ and its dual decomposition $(D^i)_{0\leq i \leq \ell}$. 

Let $e=\max\{0\leq i \leq \ell: \text{there exists $1\leq j \leq |Q|$ such that $Q_j \in V(D^i)$}\}$ ($e$ is correctly defined since $Q_0 \in V(D^0)$). 







Let $1 \leq \ind{1} \leq |Q|$ be such that $\ind{1}=\min\{1 \leq i \leq |Q|: Q_{\ind{1}} \in V(D^e)\}$ and let $\ind{2}$ such that $W_{\ind{2}}=Q_{\ind{1}}$. Now two cases may occur either $\ind{2}>p^2+p$ or $\ind{2}\leq p^2+p$.

\vspace{+0.5em}

\noindent \textbf{First case} ($\ind{2}>p^2+p$): 
see Figure \ref{fig:uwl:jail:part1} for a graphical representation of this case. Let $Q'=Q_{[1,\ind{1}]}$ and let $(B^i)_{1\leq i \leq \ell'}$ be the decomposition of $Q'$ in extremum arcs in $U$. Since $Q \cap W_{[m,+\infty]}=\emptyset$ then by lemma \ref{lem:conc:toolbox} either $P$ and $Q'$ intersect or for all $1\leq i \leq e$, there exists $1\leq j \leq \ell'$ such that arc $B^j$ dominates arc $A^i$. Now, note that for all $0\leq i \leq \ell'$, the arc $B^i+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ is an arc of $U$ and a subgraph of $P$ and then there exists $1 \leq j \leq \ell$ such that either $A^j=B^i+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ or $A^j$ dominates $B^i+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$. Now, we define a sequence of arcs $(C^i)_{1 \leq i \leq \ell''}$ of $U$ such that $C^1=A^1$ and for all $1 \leq i \leq \ell''$, if there exists $0\leq j \leq \ell'$ such that $B^j$ dominates $C^i$ then the arc $C^{i+1}$ is defined as the arc $A^{j'}$ such that either $A^{j'}=B^j+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ or $A^{j'}$ dominates $B^j+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$; if there exists no $0\leq j \leq \ell'$ such that $B^j$ dominates $C^i$ then $i=\ell''$ and $C^i$ is the last arc of the sequence. Let $\ind{3} \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $C^{\ell''}$ ends in $L_\ind{3}$ then $\ind{3}>\ind{2}$ otherwise the arc $C^{\ell''}$ would be dominated by an arc of $(B^j)_{1\leq j\leq \ell'}$. Then, for all $1 \leq i \leq \ell''$, the arc $C^i$ is a subgraph of $P$ and for all $1\leq i \leq \ell''-1$ the arc $C^{i+1}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ dominates $C^i$. For all $1\leq i \leq \ell''$, let $w_i$ be the width of arc $C^i$. 






Now, we prove by recurrence that for all $1 \leq i \leq \ell''$, the hypothesis $H(i):"$ $w_i \geq 2(i-1)$. Moreover for all $0\leq j <i $, we have $w_i\geq w_j$ and there exists $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $C^i$ ends in $L_k$ with $k\leq i(w_i)+(i-1)p"$. The arc $C^1$ is the arc $A^1$ which starts in $L_0$ and $w_1\geq 0$ and $C^1$ ends in $L_{w_1}$. Thus the initialization of the recurrence is done. Now, suppose that $H(i)$ is true for $1 \leq i \leq \ell''-1$, then $C^i$ is dominated by $C^{i+1}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$. Then there exists $\ind{4},\ind{5},\ind{6},\ind{7} \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $C^i$ starts in $L_{\ind{4}}$ and ends in $L_{\ind{5}}$ and  $C^{i+1}$ starts in $L_{\ind{6}}$ and ends in $L_{\ind{7}}$ with $\ind{6}-p<\ind{4}\leq \ind{5}<\ind{7}-p$. This means that $\ind{7}-\ind{6} \geq \ind{5}-\ind{4}+2\geq w_i+2\geq 2i$. Moreover, by recurrence we have that for all $1\leq j \leq i $, $w_{i+1} > w_i \geq w_j$. By recurrence, we have $\ind{5} \leq i(w_i)+(i-1)p$. Moreover $\ind{7}=\ind{6}+w_{i+1}$ and $\ind{6}-p<\ind{5}$ then $\ind{7} \leq i(w_i)+(i-1)p+w_{i+1}+p \leq (i+1)(w_{i+1})+ip$ and the recurrence is true. Now, if $\ell'' \geq \frac{p}{2}+1$ then $w_{\ell''}\geq p$ and by lemma \ref{lem:jail:arc}, $P$ and $Q$ intersect. Otherwise, suppose that $\ell'' \leq \frac{p}{2}$ and $w_{\ell''}<p$ then $C^{\ell'}$ ends in $L_{\ind{3}}$ with $\ind{3} < p^2+p$ which is a contradiction.

\vspace{+0.5em}

\noindent \textbf{Second case ($\ind{2}\leq p^2+p$)}: see Figure \ref{fig:uwl:jail:part2} for a graphical representation of this case.
Since $Q=P-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ then the decomposition of $Q$ in extremum arcs in $U$ is $(B^i)_{1\leq i \leq \ell}$ with for all $1\leq i \leq \ell$, $B^i=A^i-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$. Consider $1\leq i\leq \ell$ such that $B^i$ starts in $W_{\ind{8}}$ with $\ind{8} > \ind{2}$ then there exists $1\leq j \leq \ell$ such that $W_\ind{8} \in S^j$ (otherwise this would contradicts the definition of $e$) then either $A^j$ and $B^i$ intersect or $A^j$ dominates $B^i$. Now, we define a sequence of arcs $(C^i)_{1 \leq i \leq \ell'}$ of $U$ such that $C^{1}=A^\ell$ and for all $1 \leq i \leq \ell'$, if there exists $1\leq j \leq \ell$ such that $A^j$ dominates $C^i-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ then the arc $C^{i+1}$ is defined as the arc $A^{j}$; if there exists no $1\leq j \leq \ell$ such that $C^j$ dominates $C^i-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ then $i=\ell'$ and $C^i$ is the last arc of the sequence. Let $\ind{3} \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $C^{\ell'}$ starts in $L_\ind{3}$ then $\ind{3}\leq \ind{2}+p$ otherwise the arc $C^{1}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ would be dominated by an arc of $(A^j)_{1\leq j\leq \ell'}$. Then, for all $1 \leq i \leq \ell'$, the arc $C^i$ is a subgraph of $P$ and for all $1\leq i \leq \ell'-1$ the arc $C^{i+1}$ dominates $C^i-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$. For all $1\leq i \leq \ell'$, let $w_i$ be the width of arc $C^i$.





Now, we prove by recurrence that for all $1 \leq i \leq \ell'$, the hypothesis $H(i):"$ $w_i \geq 2(i-1)$. Moreover for all $1\leq j \leq i$, we have $w_i \geq w_j$ and there exists $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $C^i$ starts in $L_k$ with $k\geq m - (i(w_i)+(i-1)p)"$. The arc $C^{1}$ is the arc $A^{\ell}$ which ends in $W_{m}$ and thus $C^{1}$ starts in $W_{m-w_{\ell'}}$. Thus the initialization of the recurrence is done. Now, suppose that $H(i)$ is true for $1 \leq i \leq \ell'-1$, then $C^{i}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ is dominated by $C^{i+1}$. Then there exists $\ind{4},\ind{5},\ind{6},\ind{7} \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that $C^i$ starts in $L_{\ind{4}}$ and ends in $L_{\ind{5}}$ and  $C^{i+1}$ starts in $L_{\ind{6}}$ and ends in $L_{\ind{7}}$ with $\ind{6}<\ind{4}-p \leq \ind{5}-p < \ind{7}$. This means that $\ind{7}-\ind{6}\geq \ind{5}-\ind{4}+2\geq w_i+2\geq 2i$. Moreover, by recurrence we have that for all $1\leq i \leq j$, $w_{i+1} > w_i \geq w_j$. By recurrence, we have $\ind{4} \geq m-(i(w_i)+(i-1)p)$. Moreover $\ind{6}=\ind{7}-w_{i+1}$ and $\ind{7}>\ind{4}-p$ then $\ind{6} \geq m-(i(w_i)+(i-1)p)-w_{i+1}-p \geq m-((i+1)(w_{i+1})+ip)$ and the recurrence is true. Now, if $\ell' \geq \frac{p}{2}+1$ then $w_{1}\geq p$ and by lemma \ref{lem:jail:arc}, $P$ and $Q$ intersect. Otherwise, suppose that $\ell' \leq \frac{p}{2}$ and $w_{\ell'}<p$ then $C^{1}$ starts in $L_{\ind{3}}$ with $\ind{3} > m-p^2 \geq \ind{2}+p$ which is a contradiction.

nodes.name: Jail lemma
nodes.statement: Let P be a path assembly producible by T=(T,sigma,1) satisfying macroscopic initial conditions and 1leq ind1 leq |P|. If the path assembly P is jailed at index ind1 then it is fragile or pumpable.
assumptions: Let P be a path assembly producible by T=(T,sigma,1) satisfying macroscopic initial conditions and 1leq ind1 leq |P|.
If the path assembly P is jailed at index ind1
conclusions: then it is fragile or pumpable.
nodes.raw_latex: Let $P$ be a path assembly producible by $\mathcal{T}=(T,\sigma,1)$ satisfying macroscopic initial conditions and $1\leq \ind{1} \leq |P|$. If the path assembly $P$ is jailed at index $\ind{1}$ then it is fragile or pumpable.

Remark that by the definition of an exposed path assembly y_sigma<y_P_t, then |Q|>1. The graph Q is a path whose extremities are both visible from the west and then consider the cut (C^+,C^-) of the grid by the path Q whose extremities are both visible from the west. Let W be the window of this cut of the grid, let m=|Q|-1 and consider an indexing of the window coherent with Q (W_0=pos(Q_1) and W_m=pos(Q_|Q|)). By definition of an exposed path assembly, the output glue of P_t exits to the east and by the definition of t then pos(P_t+1) notin V(C^+). Now, for the sake of contradiction suppose that domP_[t+1,|P|] cap V(C^+) neq emptyset then let ind1=min\i>t:pos(P_i) in C^+\ then there exists ind2 in Z such that W_ind2=pos(P_ind1). If 0leq ind2 leq m then P_[1,t] and P_[t+1,|P|] intersect which contradicts the fact that P is simple. If ind2>m then pos(P_ind1-1)=(x_P_ind1,y_P_ind1+1) which contradicts the definition of t. Now, let $\ind{1}>0$ such that $W_{\ind{1}}=A^{i}_{|A^{i}|}$ and let $\ind{5} \geq n$ such that $W_{\ind{5}}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}=W_{\ind{1}}$. Also, let $\ind{4}>\ind{1}$ such that $W_{\ind{4}}=D^{i}_{|D^{i}|}$ and let $\ind{6} \geq n$ such that $W_{\ind{6}}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}=W_{\ind{4}}$. Since $(A^i)_{1\leq i \leq \ell}$ is positive then $\ind{6}> \ind{5}$. By lemma \ref{lem:decompo:path}, we have $D^i \cap (W_{[n,+\infty]} -\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}) = \{D^i_1, D^i_{|D^i|}\}= \{W_{\ind{1}},W_{\ind{4}}\}$ and then $D^i+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}} \cap W_{[n,+\infty]} = \{W_{\ind{5}},W_{\ind{6}}\}$. Now either $(D^i+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}})$ is an arc of $\mathcal{F}$ or $(D^i+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}) \cap W_{[-\infty,n-1]} \neq \emptyset$. In the first case, then $u \in E(\mathcal{F})$. nodes.statement: We prove this lemma by recurrence. Consider the following hypothesis for all 1leq i leq |D|, H(i): "either P is fragile or there exists a fork F such that the underlying path of F is D_[1,i]". First note that P_[s^+,s^+]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv is always a fork and then H(1) is true. Now, suppose that H(i) is true for 1leq i leq |D|-1. Then, by the definition of D and by the fact that the decomposition of W_[n,+infty] is positive (Lemma ), either there exists s^- leq ind3 leq |P| such that the edge (D_i,D_i+1) is equal to (P_ind3,P_ind3+1) or there exists s^+ leq ind3 leq |P| such that the edge (D_i,D_i+1) is equal to (P_ind3-ensuremathoverrightarrowv,P_ind3+1-ensuremathoverrightarrowv). See Figures of appendix for the intuition of the two following cases. Case (D_i,D_i+1)=(P_ind3,P_ind3+1): then either type(P_ind3)=type(F_|F|) or type(P_ind3)neq type(F_|F|). In the second case, since F is a fork then P_[1,s^-]cdot F is a path assembly producible by T and P is fragile. Otherwise, let F'=F cdot P_[ind3,ind3+1] which is a path assembly whose binding graph is D_[1,i+1] and by lemmas and , P_[1,s^-]cdot F' is a path assembly producible by T and by lemmas and , P_[1,s^+cdot (F'+ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is a path assembly producible by T. In this case H(i+1) is true. Case (D_i,D_i+1)=(P_ind3-ensuremathoverrightarrowv,P_ind3+1-ensuremathoverrightarrowv): then either type(P_ind3)=type(F_|F|) or type(P_ind3)neq type(F_|F|). If type(P_ind3)neq type(F_|F|), since F is a fork then P_[1,s^+]cdot (F+ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is a path assembly producible by T and P is fragile. Otherwise F'=F cdot (P_[ind3,ind3+1]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is a path assembly whose binding graph is D_[1,i+1] and by lemmas and , P_[1,s^-]cdot F' is a path assembly producible by T and by lemmas and , P_[1,s^+]cdot (F'+ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is a path assembly producible by T. In this case, H(i+1) is true. To conclude, Since H(|D|) is true, then either P is fragile or there exists a fork F such that the binding graph of F is D and in this case F is long.

We prove this lemma by recurrence. Consider the following hypothesis for all $1\leq i \leq |D|$, $H(i):$ "either $P$ is fragile or there exists a fork $F$ such that the underlying path of $F$ is $D_{[1,i]}$". First note that $P_{[s^+,s^+]}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}}$ is always a fork and then $H(1)$ is true. Now, suppose that $H(i)$ is true for $1\leq i \leq |D|-1$. Then, by the definition of $D$ and by the fact that the decomposition of $W_{[n,+\infty]}$ is positive (Lemma \ref{lem:fork:ordered}), either there exists $s^- \leq \ind{3} \leq |P|$ such that the edge $(D_i,D_{i+1})$ is equal to $(P_{\ind{3}},P_{\ind{3}+1})$ or there exists $s^+ \leq \ind{3} \leq |P|$ such that the edge $(D_i,D_{i+1})$ is equal to $(P_{\ind{3}}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}},P_{\ind{3}+1}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}})$. See Figures of appendix \ref{app:buildf} for the intuition of the two following cases.

\noindent \textbf{Case  $(D_i,D_{i+1})=(P_{\ind{3}},P_{\ind{3}+1})$}:
then either $\mathrm{type}(P_{\ind{3}})=\mathrm{type}(F_{|F|})$  or $\mathrm{type}(P_{\ind{3}})\neq \mathrm{type}(F_{|F|})$. In the second case, since $F$ is a fork then $P_{[1,s^-]}\cdot F$ is a path assembly producible by $\mathcal{T}$ and $P$ is fragile. Otherwise, let $F'=F \cdot P_{[\ind{3},\ind{3}+1]}$ which is a path assembly whose binding graph is $D_{[1,i+1]}$ and by lemmas \ref{lem:freezone} and \ref{fact:pointun}, $P_{[1,s^-]}\cdot F'$ is a path assembly producible by $\mathcal{T}$ and by lemmas \ref{lem:freezone} and \ref{lem:secondstep}, $P_{[1,s^+}\cdot (F'+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}})$ is a path assembly producible by $\mathcal{T}$. In this case $H(i+1)$ is true. 
 
\noindent \textbf{Case $(D_i,D_{i+1})=(P_{\ind{3}}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}},P_{\ind{3}+1}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}})$}: then either $\mathrm{type}(P_{\ind{3}})=\mathrm{type}(F_{|F|})$ or $\mathrm{type}(P_{\ind{3}})\neq \mathrm{type}(F_{|F|})$. If $\mathrm{type}(P_{\ind{3}})\neq \mathrm{type}(F_{|F|})$, since $F$ is a fork then $P_{[1,s^+]}\cdot (F+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}})$ is a path assembly producible by $\mathcal{T}$ and $P$ is fragile. Otherwise $F'=F \cdot (P_{[\ind{3},\ind{3}+1]}-\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}})$ is a path assembly whose binding graph is $D_{[1,i+1]}$ and by lemmas \ref{lem:freezone} and \ref{fact:pointun}, $P_{[1,s^-]}\cdot F'$ is a path assembly producible by $\mathcal{T}$ and by lemmas \ref{lem:freezone} and \ref{lem:secondstep}, $P_{[1,s^+]}\cdot (F'+\ensuremath{\overrightarrow{v}})$ is a path assembly producible by $\mathcal{T}$. In this case, $H(i+1)$ is true. 
  
To conclude, Since $H(|D|)$ is true, then either $P$ is fragile or there exists a fork $F$ such that the binding graph of $F$ is $D$ and in this case $F$ is long.

nodes.statement: This proof is in three parts. In the first one, we define an infinite path which will be useful to split the free zone. In the second part, we show that this path is indeed a subgraph of the free zone. In the last part, we show that the last intersection between this path and P_[s^+,|P|] is a dominant tile. See Figure for an illustration of this proof. vspace+0.5em Definition: let ensuremathoverrightarrowv=overrightarrowP_s^-P_s^+, let F be the free zone of P associated to P_[s^-,s^+] and W be its window, let p=x_ensuremathoverrightarrowv+y_ensuremathoverrightarrowv. Consider a coherent indexing of this window. Consider the height function h of direction ensuremathoverrightarrowv. Let H=max\h(pos(P_i)): s^- leq i leq |P| and y_P_igeq y_P_s^-\. Let (D^H,U^H) be the the cut of the grid by the line of direction ensuremathoverrightarrowv and height H and let L^H be its window. Now, since the height of P_s^- is less than H then the infinite line W_[-infty,0] intersects with L^H. Consider an indexing of L^H such that L^H_0 in W_[-m,0], L^H_1 notin W_[-m,0] and L^H_p=L^H_0+ensuremathoverrightarrowv. Now, let H'=max\h(pos(P_i)): s^- leq i leq |P| and there exists kgeq 0 such that y_P_i=y_P_s^-+ky_ensuremathoverrightarrowv\. By definition H'leq H. Now, we define the path R as follow: we definite the positions A and B such that y_A=y_P_s^- and h(A)=H' and B=A+(0,1) then R is the concatenation of the four paths R^1cdot R^2 cdot R^3 cdot R^4 defined as: item R^1 is the path such that R^1_1=L^H_0, R^1_|R^1|=A and for all 1leq i leq |R^1|-1, we have R^1_i+1=R^1_i+(1,0); item R^2 is the path from A to B (R^2 is made of two vertices and one edges); item R^3 is the path such that R^3_1=B, R^3_|R^3|=L^H_1 and for all 1leq i leq |R^1|-1, we have R^3_i+1=R^3_i-(1,0); item R^4 is the path L^H_[1,p]. vspace+0.5em noindentThe path omeplusR is a subgraph of F: If L^H_[0,+infty] is a not subgraph of F then there exists s^- leq ind1 leq |P| such that h(pos(P_ind1))>H and y_P_ind1>P_s^- which contradicts the definition of H. Now if omeplusR is not a subgraph of F then there exists s^- leq ind1 leq |P| and kgeq 0 such that y_P_ind1=y_P_s^-+ky_ensuremathoverrightarrowv and x_P_ind1>x_A+kx_ensuremathoverrightarrowv which contradicts the definition of H'. vspace+0.5em noindentThere exists a dominant tile: let Q=omeplusR, by definition of R and H' there exists an index ind3 in N and kgeq0 such that Q_ind3 in domP_[s^-,|P|] and y_Q_ind3 = y_P_s^-+kensuremathoverrightarrowv. Note that if k=0 then since P_s^- is visible from the west, we have Q_ind3=pos(P_s^-). In this case, Q_ind3+|R|-1=P_s^+ and then we can suppose that k>0 and that ind3geq |R|. Remark that V(Q_[|R|,+infty]) cap V(W_[m,+infty])=emptyset otherwise we would have y_P_|P|geq y_P_[s^-,|P|]+y_ensuremathoverrightarrowv which contradicts the definition of a U-turn. Now, let ind4=max\i: Q_i in V(W_[0,+infty])\. By definition ind4 geq ind3 geq |R| and then y_Q_ind4 geq y_P_s^+. Also, since V(Q_[|R|,+infty]) cap V(W_[m,+infty])=emptyset, there exists s^- leq dleq |P| such that P_d=Q_ind4. Now if d < s^+ then let (G_1,G_2) be the cut of the grid by the underlying path of P_[s^-,s^+] whose extremities are both visible from the west and let W' be its window. Consider an indexing of W' coherent with P_[s^-,s^+] and suppose that G_1 is the left side of W', thus G_1 is a subgraph of F. Then Q_ind4 belongs to G_1. Moreover, since y_Q_ind4 geq y_s^+, since Q_ind4neq pos(P_s^+) and since Q is a subgraph of F then Q_[ind4,+infty] is a subgraph of G_1. But Y_G_1=Y_P_[s^-,s^+] is finite which contradicts the definition of Q. Then, dgeq s^+ and let C=Q_[ind4,ind4+|R|-1]. Since Q is a subgraph of F and by definition of ind4, then omeplusC splits the free zone into (F^-,F^+). Moreover Q_[0,ind4] is a subgraph of F such that Q_0 in W_[-infty,0] and then Q_[0,ind4] is a subgraph of F^-. Since ind4 geq |R| then C-ensuremathoverrightarrowv=Q_[ind4-|R|+1,ind4] is a subgraph of F^- and thus P_d is a dominant tile.

Consider $\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3 \in \mathbb{Z}$ such $\ell_2\geq \ell_1$ and $\ell_3 \geq f^s(\ell_2+1)$. Suppose that $\dom{\sigma} \subset \mathcal{R}(\ell_1)$ then if there exists $1\leq \ind{3} \leq \ind{4} \leq |P|$ such that $\mathrm{pos}(P_\ind{3}) \notin \mathcal{R}(\ell_3)$ and $\mathrm{pos}(P_{\ind{4}}) \in \mathcal{R}(\ell_1)$ then either $P$ is pumpable or fragile or there exists $1\leq \ind{1} \leq \ind{2} \leq \ind{3}$ such that $\mathrm{pos}(P_{\ind{1}}) \notin \mathcal{R}(\ell^2)$ and $\mathrm{pos}(P_{\ind{2}}) \in \mathcal{R}(\ell^1)$. Consider a path assembly $P$ satisfying macroscopic initial conditions and producible by $\mathcal{T}=(T,\sigma,1)$. nodes.statement: This proof is done in three steps. During the first step, we initialize different tools (seed constraint, fork) to set up a good setting. During the second step, we build the first stake and during the third one we build the second stake. Several incidents may occurs during the construction of the stakes but anyone of these problems leads to the fragility or pumpability of~P. vspace+0.5em Initialization: see Figures and for an illustration of this part of the proof. By the seed lemma (lemma ), we have domsigma subset R(B^sigma) or P is fragile or pumpable. By lemma , either P is fragile or pumpable or there exists 1leq s^-< s^+ leq ind4 such that P_[s^-,s^+] is a visible candidate segment of direction ensuremathoverrightarrowv such that ||ensuremathoverrightarrowv||leq B and domP_[1,s^+] subset R(B^v). By the definition of macroscopic initial conditions, there exists 1leq ind4 leq |P| such that ind4=min\i:y_P_i = f^r(B^v+B)+B+1)\. Note that s^+ leq ind4 and remark that by definition of ind4, the path assembly P_[1,ind4] is an exposed path assembly (with a turn back of Y_P_[1,ind4]). Now either domP_[1,ind4] subset R(f^b(f^r(B^v+B)+B+1)) or not. In the second the case, P_[1,ind4] fits in a band and by lemma , P is fragile or pumpable. Otherwise, domP_[1,ind4] subset R(f^b(f^r(B^v+B)+B+1)) and by applying lemma to P_[1,ind4], either P is fragile or pumpable or there exists a fork F such that y_F_|F|+y_ensuremathoverrightarrowvgeq f^r(B^v+B)+B+1 and domF subset R(f^b(f^r(B^v+B)+B+1) +B). Since ||ensuremathoverrightarrowv||leq B, we have y_F_|F| geq f^r(B^v+B)+1. vspace+0.5em Finding the first stake: By definition of F, there exists ind1 such that ind1=min\i:y_F_i=f^r(B^v+B)+1\. By definition of a fork, there exists 1 leq ind2 leq ind4 such that F_ind1=P_ind2 or F_ind1=P_ind2-ensuremathoverrightarrowv. We suppose that F_ind1=P_ind2-ensuremathoverrightarrowv (the other case is symmetric). Remark that y_P_ind2geq f^r(B^v+B)+1 and thus pos(P_ind2) notin R(f^r(B^v+B)+1). Now, two cases occur either P_[1,s^-]cdot F_[1,ind1] cdot (P_[ind2,|P|]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is a path assembly producible by T or not. In the second case, since by definition of a fork, the path assembly P_[1,s^-]cdot F is producible by T, then P_[ind2,|P|]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv creates a collision with either F_[1,ind1] or P_[1,s^-] cup sigma. If P_[ind2,|P|]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv creates a collision with F_[1,ind1] (see Figures and ), by definition of a fork the path assembly P_[1,s^+]cdot (F+ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is producible by T and this path assembly creates a collision with P_[ind2,|P|] and thus P is fragile. If P_[ind2,|P|]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv creates a collision with P_[1,s^-] cup sigma (see Figures and ), there exists ind2 leq ind3 leq |P| such that pos(P_ind3)-ensuremathoverrightarrowv in R(B^v) and thus pos(P_ind3) in R(B^v+B). Then P does not satisfies the reset constraint for B^v+B and by the reset lemma , P is fragile or pumpable. Then, the path assembly P_[1,s^-]cdot F_[1,ind1] cdot P_[ind2,|P|]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv is producible by T (see Figure ). Let S^-= P_[1,s^-] cdot F_[1,ind1] be the first stake. Moreover, since B^-=f^b(f^r(B^v+B)+B+1)+B, then domS^- subset R(B^-). vspace+0.5em Finding the second stake: see Figure for an illustration of this part of the proof. By definition of index ind4 and since ind2leq ind4, there exist two indices ind2 leq ind5 leq |P| and ind5 leq ind8 leq |P| such that ind5=min\i geq ind2: pos(P_i) notin R(f^r(B^-+B))\ and ind8=min\i geq ind5: pos(P_i) notin R(f^j(f^r(B^-+B+1))\. Then either P_[ind5,ind8]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv and P_[ind5,ind8] intersect or not. In the second case, since domP_[1,ind5] subset R(f^r(B^-+B+1)) then by the jail lemma (lemma ), P is fragile or pumpable. In the second case, there exists ind5 leq ind6leq ind8 and ind5 leq ind7 leq ind8 such that ind6=min\i geq ind5:pos(P_i)-ensuremathoverrightarrowv in domP_[ind5,ind8]\ and pos(P_ind7)=pos(P_ind6)-ensuremathoverrightarrowv. Moreover, domP_[ind2,ind6] subset R(f^j(f^r(B^-+B+1))+1). Now, since S^- cdot (P_[ind2,ind6]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is producible by T then either P is fragile or P_ind7=P_ind6-ensuremathoverrightarrowv and then P_ind7+ensuremathoverrightarrowv=P_ind6. Then either P_[1,ind6] cdot (P_[ind7,|P|]+ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is a path assembly producible by P or not. In the first case S^+=P_[1,ind6] is our second stake and the lemma is true since domS^+ subset R(f^j(f^r(B^-+B+1))+B+1) and B^s=f^j(f^r(B^-+B+1))+B+1 (see Figure ). Otherwise, P_[ind7,|P|]+ensuremathoverrightarrowv collides with P_[1,ind6] cup sigma. If the collision occurs between P_[ind7,|P|]+ensuremathoverrightarrowv and P_[1,ind2] cup sigma then there exists ind7 leq ind9 leq |P| such that pos(P_ind9+ensuremathoverrightarrowv) in R(B^-) and then pos(P_ind9) in R(B^-+B) (see Figures and ). Since ind9geq ind7 geq ind5 and since pos(P_ind5) notin R(f^r(B^-+B)) then P does not satisfies the reset constraint for B^-+B and by the reset lemma , P is fragile or pumpable. Otherwise there exists a collision between P_[ind7,|P|]+ensuremathoverrightarrowv and P_[ind2,ind6] and then there exists a collision between P_[ind7,|P|] and P_[ind2,ind6]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv (see Figures and ). Since S^- cdot (P_[ind2,ind6]-ensuremathoverrightarrowv) is producible by T then P is fragile.
